Jonas / team — quick notes from initial triage:
- Autoscaling: both us-west and us-east pools scaled but with a delay — infra shows upscales triggered ~30s after the traffic inflection. Peak CPU/GPU utilization reached ~92% before new nodes came up.
- Batching: we observed a short burst of synchronous single-request batches (small prompt % increase) which increases overhead per token.
- KV cache: several requests missed local KV cache due to session affinity churn during the surge (we saw repeated cold-KV loads).
- Model fallback: no model fallback events recorded. No recent model rollout in hours.

Temporary mitigations we recommend to customer immediately (low friction):
1) reduce streaming buffer (enable smaller chunk interval) — reduces perceived per-chunk latency
2) if acceptable, fall back to non-streamed generate for agents with heavy contexts for the next 45 minutes
3) set a short client-side retry for WS connect (250ms jitter)

I'll keep digging into kernel selection logs and autoscaler logs.

Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime chat p99 spikes — urgent ops/eng attention

Quick findings from the serving runtime and kernel logs:
- Around 13:04 PT we saw a pattern of longer kernel schedule latencies on 2 x A100 pools (us-west) — median kernel schedule ~30ms -> spikes up to 220ms for some attention kernels.
- Several worker processes hit a transient backpressure condition while a rolling GC landed (we have a maintenance GC sweep every 6 hours; it overlapped with their peak).
- KV cache churn: session affinity lost due to LB rehash during scale caused ~18% of requests to rehydrate cache across nodes.
- We saw a small but noticeable rise in quantized fallback paths for a microsubset (0.6% of requests) — these executed slower kernels.

Immediate action items taken:
- Temporarily increased pre-warm pool for us-west by +8 instances (approx +20% headroom) — live now.
- Disabled a non-critical background GC on the affected pool to avoid further overlap during this window.
- Pushed a canary route to route 20% of traffic to a lower-latency model variant (reduced context size) as automated fallback — rolling in last 10m.

I'll prepare an ops postmortem doc; need to run a replay to confirm the GC overlap effect.

Laura
Head of Platform Reliability

Alicia —

Thanks for the details and the logs. Short update on what we've done and recommended temporary mitigations for you to apply immediately:
- We've temporarily increased pre-warmed capacity in us-west and disabled the GC sweep that overlapped your peak. You should see p99 regressions reduce within ~10–15 minutes as warm instances absorb load.
- Suggested temporary client-side settings: reduce streaming chunk size to 50–100ms, or if that's not viable, switch the heaviest agent sessions to non-streamed generate for the next 1 hour.
- If you want us to flip a feature flag on the account to force non-stream fallback for sessions > 60s, we can push that and roll it back after traffic subsides.

ETA for a full postmortem: we will have a preliminary RCA within 24 hours and a full write-up within 72 hours.

I'll keep this thread updated.

— Sean

Next steps we commit to:
1) 24h preliminary RCA (in progress) — will include timeline, autoscaler latency analysis, and GC scheduling conflict evidence.

3) Offer KiteWave an account-level flag to force non-stream fallback for long sessions during known marketing events (opt-in) + a one-time credit for the service impact.
